precepts.text: Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.
precepts.point: Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God: that's what Moses did. Than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season: cuz if anybody say sin ain't pleasurable, that's a lie. It's very fun. But you got to perform abstinence.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
Moses chose “rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” What is the sin he refused? John defines it: “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.”

Sin is breaking God’s law. The pleasures of sin are the pleasures of transgressing the law, and if anybody says sin isn’t pleasurable, that’s a lie. It is very fun. But you have to perform abstinence, and choose affliction with the people of God over it, the way Moses did.

That is the difference between Moses and the hireling. A hireling has a temporary time in this truth. He or she doesn’t care about salvation, and is willing to destroy the family, the brotherhood, everything they built up, just for their own sin. The love of sin. The hireling chooses the pleasure of transgressing the law for a season; the true servant chooses to suffer with the people of God.

precepts.text: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.
precepts.point: Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God: that's what Moses did. Than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season: cuz if anybody say sin ain't pleasurable, that's a lie. It's very fun. But you got to perform abstinence.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
The pleasures of sin last only “for a season”, and Paul shows where they end: “That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.”

If anybody says sin isn’t pleasurable, that’s a lie; it is very fun. That is exactly why it is dangerous. Those who have pleasure in unrighteousness instead of believing the truth are the ones who are damned. So you have to perform abstinence.

Moses saw it. He chose “rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” The hireling does the opposite. He has a temporary time in this truth and does not care about salvation. He or she is willing to destroy the family, the brotherhood and everything they built up, just for their own sin, for the love of sin. That love of sin is having pleasure in unrighteousness, and its end is damnation.

precepts.text: Without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
The reward of Colossians 2:18 is for those who come to God by faith: “But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.”

God is a rewarder, and he rewards those that diligently seek him. Christ said his reward is with him “to give every man according as his work shall be”, and here we see it is faith that pleases him and diligent seeking that he rewards.

So when Paul says “Let no man beguile you of your reward”, this is what is at stake. The men beguiling the believers were turning them away from faith in Christ, back to the carnal ordinances, putting Moses over Christ and animal sacrifice over the sacrifice of Christ. Without faith it is impossible to please God, so a man who talks you out of your faith in Christ is talking you out of your reward.

precepts.text: Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season. That pleasure is just for a season, and you're going to pay the price for it. Your mind has convinced you it is pleasure because you've made an agreement with your eyes to continue looking. That's what got David caught up: he did not look away, and it brought all the other problems that came with it.
precepts.point: Turning your head away is proof you have control of your members: that's called self-control. But if you can't turn away, Christ is not the captain of that ship; Satan is running the show. When you see something inappropriate online and you find yourself clicking and looking, you're not in control; you're on the rabbit hole looking for that feel-good, because sin feels good.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
Sirach says “Turn away thine eye from a beautiful woman”, and it begins with the eyes. Your eyes are directly correlated with your mind; they work in sync, and what you see makes your mind react a certain way. When you see something inappropriate online, not even porn, which is obvious, but something you know is not right, and you find yourself clicking and looking, you are not in control. You are down that rabbit hole looking for that feel good, because sin feels good. It is enjoyable.

That is why Moses is set before us in Hebrews: “Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”. The pleasure of sin is only for a season, and you are going to pay the price for it. There is a price that is going to be paid.

That little season we deem as pleasure is only pleasure because your mind has convinced you it is, and that is because you have made an agreement with your eyes to keep looking. That is what got David caught up. He did not look away, and it brought all the other problems that came along with it.

So the best thing to do is turn away. Turning your head is proof you have control of your members; that is called self-control. If you cannot turn away, Christ is not the captain of that ship; Satan is driving. “For many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman”, deceived because they looked and did not turn away, when a simple motion of the head could have saved them a world of problems. Moses chose affliction with the people of God over the pleasure; that is the choice set before us.

precepts.text: The officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten. The taskmasters set officers of our own people over us. In America those are called house negroes; in ancient Egypt they were called officers. Some of them had a good living, until the beatings came to them too.
precepts.point: Some of our people in ancient Egypt had money and high standing, and they were okay with the oppression they were living under. It is the same thing today: the celebrities, the entertainers, the pastors with money that are comfortable here in modern day Egypt. When a people live in oppression for centuries, oppression becomes a norm; you watch at it as a way of life. That is why the scripture talks about us trusting in the shadow of Egypt, trusting in oppression.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
Moses “refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God”. Understand that in ancient Egypt everybody was not bad off. Things were not bad for Moses; Moses made things bad for himself by killing the Egyptian, and there was a consequence for killing an Egyptian, so Moses was on the run.

Exodus 5:14 shows that some of our own people were set up over us: “And the officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, and demanded, Wherefore have ye not fulfilled your task in making brick both yesterday and to day, as heretofore?” The taskmasters set officers of the children of Israel over us. In ancient Egypt they were called officers; in America they are called Uncle Tom Negroes, house Negroes.

To be an officer you were making money. Some of our people in ancient Egypt had money and high standing, a form of good living, and they were okay with the oppression they were going through, until the officers started getting their behinds whooped too.

It is the same thing today: Beyoncé, Usher, the pastor praying for Trump, people with money who are comfortable here in modern day Egypt, spiritual Egypt. When a people live in oppression for centuries, oppression becomes a norm and you take it as a way of life. That is why the scripture talks about us trusting in the shadow of Egypt, trusting in oppression. Moses had that comfort and refused it, choosing to suffer affliction with the people of God.

precepts.text: Moses refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, choosing affliction with the people of God over the pleasures of sin for a season. He gave up status in Egypt, so the nice job is no excuse. This is temporary; be robotic and get the feelings out of it, because feelings get you killed.
precepts.point: Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure. Many of you see America as a gorgeous woman and are mesmerized; every pleasure is available in her. Many brothers fall by harlots, and you do not have to pick up a prostitute to be dealing with the mother of all harlots.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
Don’t stumble at the beauty of the woman, America, or desire her for pleasure. Moses shows the way: “By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.” He wanted nothing to do with Egypt or the king of Egypt, because he knew he was an Israelite and God had chosen him for a mighty work, to deliver his people out of captivity.

Some of y’all say, it’s not that bad, and you show it by your mentality and your actions. Moses lived it up and had status in Egypt, like some of you have nice jobs and status in America. So you can’t say it’s because of that. Moses gave it all up; why can’t you?

“Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” For a season means it is temporary. It is only here for so long, and then destruction and salvation. That is the mindset we have to have.

We have to be robotic and get the feelings out of it. Nobody cares how you feel; feelings get you killed. Choose affliction with the people of God over the passing pleasures of Babylon.

precepts.text: Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. Substance is what you can touch. The student crossing campus with his T-squares and architect tubes has no degree yet, but the works of his mind tell you where he is going; that is how faith is validated by action. The Lord called the earth earth while it was without form and void because it existed in his mind, then the Spirit moved on the elements and formed it, and he compared the light to what he imagined and saw that it was good. Sisters do the same in the mirror, and walk away when the image matches the one in their mind. That is the power we have, and our elders were cut off from teaching us basics like that.
precepts.point: Our people in the world are raised to be slaves and statistics, fuel for the oppressor; when they see people who look like them building families, businesses, and healing on every level, they ask how, and you answer with the hope of your gospel: I was in a mess like you. When you come through these doors the brothers say welcome home, and I felt it: I never knew I was not home until I got there, and only then did the whole landscape make sense.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders & Fathers: the Children Are Listening

precepts.why:
“What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?” Can words save him? Because that is basically all you are giving. Some people don’t even understand what faith really is, because faith alone is just saying I believe in something. Paul defines it: “Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.”

So don’t tell me you have faith. Faith is the substance, and substance is what you can touch, what you can see, something materialized. You can have faith in your head all day long, underneath your skull; I can’t see it. The only way I will know what is in your mind is when I see action as a result of your thinking. As a man thinks, you are supposed to see the fruit of it.

Even if he or she has not achieved it yet, you can tell where they are going by how they carry themselves. On a college campus you see a student walking into the engineering building with his T-squares and architect tubes. He doesn’t have the degree yet, he is not an architect or engineer yet, but the works of his mind tell you where he is going. That is how faith is validated by action. Where there is no vision, the people perish; your mind has to manipulate the elements around you to form what you have in your head.

That is what the Lord did. The earth was without form and void, meaning it did not exist yet, but he still called it earth, because earth existed in God’s mind. Then the Spirit moved upon the face of the waters, the elements, and caused them to form the earth and the light. And he saw that the light was good: he compared what was formed to what he imagined and it agreed with the thought in his mind. Sisters do the same at the mirror; you don’t walk away until what you did with your hands matches the image in your mind, and then you say it is good. That is the power we have, but our elders were cut off from giving us basic understanding like that, and we fell asleep for centuries.

That is why the elders must set up organizational foundations, literal buildings where people can see the works of the teaching. A brother or sister naked and destitute of daily food told “Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled”, but given nothing, is still hungry. That is church, that is Christianity. “Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.”

precepts.text: Faith is the evidence of things not seen; with Noah the thing not seen was rain.
precepts.point: As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back; that takes the same faith. In the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, and marrying until Noah entered the ark and there was no more chance to repent; so shall the coming of the Son of man be. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

note.label: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark

precepts.why:
“Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.” Noah did it by faith. “Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.”

With Noah the thing not seen was rain. Up to that time rain had never been seen, and it takes faith to build an ark for a thing that has never happened. That is the faith we must have to prepare our households for when Christ comes back.

precepts.text: By faith Noah, warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear and prepared an ark to the saving of his house.
precepts.point: As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back; that takes the same faith. In the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, and marrying until Noah entered the ark and there was no more chance to repent; so shall the coming of the Son of man be. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

note.label: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark

precepts.why:
Paul says “without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.” Noah pleased the Most High because he did all that was commanded him by faith.

“By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house”. The thing not seen as yet was rain; it had never happened, and he built anyway. By that ark “he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.”

As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back, and that takes the same faith. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

precepts.text: Through faith Sara received strength to conceive past age, because she judged Him faithful who had promised; of one as good as dead sprang as many as the stars.
precepts.point: Is any thing too hard for the Lord? The barren woman is made a joyful mother of children. Through faith Sarah received strength to conceive when she was past age, and Abraham, as good as dead at a hundred, staggered not at the promise but was strong in faith, fully persuaded that what He had promised He was able to perform.

note.label: Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom

precepts.why:
“Through faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed, and was delivered of a child when she was past age, because she judged him faithful who had promised.” She laughed at first, but she came to judge Him faithful, and nothing was too hard for the Lord.

“Therefore sprang there even of one, and him as good as dead, so many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable.” Abraham was as good as dead at a hundred, and Sarah past age, and out of the two of them came a people that cannot be numbered.

precepts.text: By faith Abraham offered up Isaac, accounting that God was able to raise him up even from the dead.
precepts.point: Abraham's inner faith carried him: he accounted that God was able to raise Isaac up, even from the dead, since the promise stood in Isaac who had no children yet. Faith and the commandments go together; you cannot have one without the other.

note.label: Genesis 22: The Offering of Isaac

precepts.why:
What carried Abraham to the point of the knife was his inner faith. “By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac: and he that had received the promises offered up his only begotten son, Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called.”

The promise stood in Isaac, and Isaac had no children yet. So Abraham accounted “that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure.” He did not withhold his son because he believed God could raise him up and still keep the promise.

That faith and his obedience were one thing. Faith and the commandments go together; you cannot have one without the other, and Abraham had both on that altar.

precepts.text: By faith Jacob blessed the sons of Joseph, and by faith Joseph gave commandment concerning his bones.
precepts.point: Neither was there a man born like unto Joseph, a governor of his brethren, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of the Lord. To grow in spirit and be like him, put on the spirit of the forefathers.

note.label: Genesis 47: Goshen, the Famine, and the Fifth Part

precepts.why:
“By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff. By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel; and gave commandment concerning his bones.”

That is this scene: Israel, with the time drawn nigh that he must die, making Joseph swear to carry him out of Egypt and bury him in the buryingplace of his fathers, and bowing himself upon the bed’s head. It was faith. And Joseph took the same faith to his own death, making mention of the departing of the children of Israel and giving commandment concerning his bones.

Hebrews 11 is the hall of faith, the faithful men of the sons of God, a chapter to read.

precepts.text: By faith his parents hid him, because they saw he was a proper child, and they were not afraid of the king's commandment.
precepts.point: The woman conceived and bare a son, and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months. Goodly means the child was exceeding fair; there was something special about this child from his birth.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

precepts.why:
“By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king’s commandment.”

Goodly, exceeding fair, a proper child: the same thing. His parents saw there was something special about this child from his birth, and it was by faith they hid him three months, not afraid of the king’s commandment.

precepts.text: By faith Moses refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, esteemed the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt, and forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king.
precepts.point: The same claim stands now: the remnant does not want the names of the captivity but the natural heritage of Israel, esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of this land.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

precepts.why:
Pharaoh sought to slay Moses, and Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Midian. Hebrews shows what Moses gave up in that flight: “By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”.

Moses gave up his whole upbringing and position. In Egypt his head was shaved, his beard cut, his dress and customs Egyptian. He laid all of it down to be what he was called to be, an Israelite, “Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.”

“By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.” Pharaoh sought to slay him, and he fled, but not in fear of the king.

The same claim stands now. The remnant does not want the names of the captivity but the natural heritage of Israel, esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of this land.

precepts.text: By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace; her fear of the Lord worked faith, and that faith saved her.
precepts.point: Faith and fear go hand in hand. Rahab knew the Lord is not to be played with when it comes to this people, and that fear is what gave her the faith to put her life on the line. She might get caught by her king for hiding the spies, but what she really feared was the judgment of their God if she did not help them.

note.label: Joshua 2: Rahab and the Spies

precepts.why:
“By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace.” Faith and fear go hand in hand. Rahab knew the Lord is not to be played with when it comes to this people, and that fear is what gave her the faith to put her life on the line.

She might get caught by her king for hiding the spies, but what she really feared was the judgment of their God if she did not help them. Her fear of the Lord worked faith, and that faith saved her: she received the spies with peace and did not perish with the rest of Jericho that believed not.

precepts.text: Without faith it is impossible to please him; you must believe he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.
precepts.point: He shall reward evil unto mine enemies; cut them off in thy truth. Vengeance belongs to the Most High, not to us.

note.label: Psalm 54: Save Me by Thy Name

precepts.why: “But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.” David says “He shall reward evil unto mine enemies” by faith. You must believe he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him. Leaving the vengeance to him takes that faith: believing he will reward, both the diligent and the enemies.

precepts.text: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen; we believe in the promises of the Bible.
precepts.point: He shall reward evil unto mine enemies; cut them off in thy truth. Vengeance belongs to the Most High, not to us.

note.label: Psalm 54: Save Me by Thy Name

precepts.why: “Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.” We believe in the promises of the Bible. David had not yet seen his enemies cut off when he wrote “He shall reward evil unto mine enemies”, but faith is the evidence of things not seen. Vengeance is the Most High's, and we hold the promise that he will repay as substance, even before we see it.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 8 A Star Called Wormwood

precepts.why:
Be even as pilgrims upon the earth. “These all died in faith,” Our forefathers that preceded us, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, the twelve patriarchs, they all died in faith. “not having received the promises,” They didn't receive the promise of the kingdom. “but having seen them afar off,” They saw them afar off, meaning in spirit they believed it. “and were persuaded of them,” They were persuaded in faith that those things were so that were told to them. “and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.” You see what the forefathers did: they confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on earth. That is what we have to confess. A lot of us believe America is the promised land; examine how black people and Latinos think, they think America is the promised land. No: this is the land of oppression, this is the land of our captivity. We were brought here not to remain here forever; we were brought here to serve out our sentence and repent, and then be delivered from here. Pilgrims, because our forefathers were always going here, going there, going everywhere. Why? Doing the work, spreading the gospel, prophesying what was to come, preparing the people for the battle, like Ezra said.

“For they that say such things declare plainly that they seek a country.” Our people ain't seeking a country; only the prophets, us, are seeking a country, and America is not that country. “And truly, if they had been mindful of that country from whence they came out,” If our forefathers, especially the rebellious ones, had been mindful of where we came from, “they might have had opportunity to have returned.” They might have had an opportunity to return to the promised land. “But now they desire a better country,” We have read about the promised land, but now we desire a better one, “that is, an heavenly:” Because when the new kingdom is established, it tells you there are going to be twelve angels at twelve gates, and on the twelve gates the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, and the twelve foundations the names of the twelve apostles, and only the Israelites will enter into that kingdom; and there will be no temple, because the Lord will be the temple. That is what we are seeking. “wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he hath prepared for them a city.” The New Jerusalem.

points: By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death: taken up the same way Elijah was taken up. Before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.

points: By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet: what things were unseen? Heavy rain for 40 days and 40 nights, the whole earth being flooded, everyone dead on earth. That's unseen, unheard of. The Lord said, listen, Noah, I'm gonna kill everybody: get the animals, clean and unclean, get your wife, your sons and their wives, get in the boat, let's go. No problem, Lord. He had no questions; he was faithful like Abraham was.

Moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world: because Noah got saved and everybody else didn't. And became heir of the righteousness which is by faith: Noah kept the commandments of God, and by faith he built that boat. That was his works; his faith was proven by him building the ark in the first place. Faith without works is dead.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him. If you have faith, you cannot be bashful; brothers will know where you stand.

One more thing on the quiet, shy, timid brother: you do not know what he is thinking. When you are at war next to a brother like that, holding sentry, how do you know he is not going to run on you when trouble comes? You do not. So it is a deceitful spirit; they hide in the cut. note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: If we are going to allow the little tribulations to take us off the mark, think about our forefathers in chattel slavery, and think about if they would have given up. They did not have anything near the opportunities you have today. It took a great level of faith for them to persevere through years of slavery and evil treatment, with a vision in mind that one day we are going to get out of this.

Record recounted in class: the husband and wife in the slave quarters who could not protect one another from the slave master's abuse, and still had to console each other and keep going. That is trauma upon trauma, and they endured it sober, without a bottle, and still preserved a generation.

Now faith is the substance of things hoped for: our people in slavery were hoping for freedom, and faith helped them persevere through tunnels of darkness where they saw no light in sight. Faith is also the evidence of things not seen: what they hoped for was not even in their reachable grasp, but it pulled them through, like Joseph in captivity. Joseph did not know that after nearly fourteen years he would be brought out, but he knew that there is a God, and said I will stay here until he decides when to deal with me.

They persevered not knowing when the deliverance was going to come. But here we are. We get a little bit of trouble here and there and all of a sudden we cannot cope; we need alcohol, we need drugs, we need illicit things to take our mind off our problems. Our brothers and sisters could not do that. This is how we have to start putting ourselves in discipline. That is the word: discipline.
